# dsh-progress-rules

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) bundle plugin that
makes agents report progress instead of silently running
dozens of tool steps.
English | 中文
## What it does
Two independent layers, both mounted by one bundle row:

1. **System-prompt section** — `user:progress-rules` at order `10150` (after the Web surface
section

, before the deployment persona suffix). It carries your process-discipline rules and
is re-rendered

on every request, so conversation compaction can never summarize it away.
It uses its own section n

ame, so a preset's `@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona` row cannot shadow it
the way it shadows the deployment

s `@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona` row cannot shadow it
the way it shadows the deployment `personaSuffix`.

2. **Deterministic nudge** — on every `agent/pre-step`, the plugin checks whether the previous
assis

tant message contained any text block. If it only carried tool calls (or reasoning),
that step count

s as *silent*. After `everySteps` consecutive silent steps it injects one
user-role reminder into th

e next admitted step: "you ran tools without reporting, narrate in
1–3 sentences before continuing".

The reminder is a durable context message rendered as a
`progress-rules` context row, not as a mess

age from the user. Any narrated step resets the
counter.

The first layer is advisory for the model. The second layer is what actually breaks the
"40 silent s

teps" pattern, because the harness inserts the reminder itself instead of trusting
the model to reme

n, because the harness inserts the reminder itself instead of trusting
the model to remember a rule.
## Install
DSH plugins are installed into a **profile** (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>`), not globally:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then add the bundle to the profile's `package.json` (order matters: bundles compose in list
order, s
o put it after the base bundles):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Restart DSH afterwards. If your DSH build ships the `dsh plugin` command, adding the dependency
and
the bundles entry is what that command does for you.
## Configuration
The bundle patch (`cordis.patch.yml` inside this package) declares one row:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Override it from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` by targeting the same row id. Patch semantics
repl
ace the **whole** row config, so restate every key you keep:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `text` | bundled Chinese rules | System-prompt section text. Empty drops the section. |
| `name` |

`user:progress-rules` | Section name. |
| `order` | `10150` | Section order (WEB_SURFACE is 10100,

persona suffix 10200). |
| `enforce` | `true` | `false` disables the per-step nudge, leaving only th

e prompt section. |
| `reminder` | bundled one-liner | Text injected before a silent step. Empty dis

ables the nudge. |
| `everySteps` | `5` | Consecutive silent steps before one reminder. `1` = every
step, larger = quieter. |
## Why not AGENTS.md or `personaSuffix`?

- **`AGENTS.md`** is loaded as a durable user message in conversation history. On long tasks DSH
com

paction may summarize it away; the system prompt is never compacted.
- **`system-prompt.personaSuffi

x`** is shadowed for preset sessions: the shipped Standard / PTC /
Minimal presets mount `@deepseek-

ai/dsh-persona`, which registers the same
`deployment:persona-suffix` section with empty text, hidin

g the deployment value. A differently
named section avoids that entirely.
## Compatibility

- Tested with DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`, Standard preset, `deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017-cloud`.
- Plain ESM, no C

ordis imports, no runtime dependencies; uses `node:crypto`.
- The nudge detects silence by checking

text blocks in the last assistant message. A provider
that reports assistant text in a custom block
type would not be recognized — open an issue.
